subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be denied `sessions.patch` access to every legacy ownerless row, matching the existing exact-owner delete boundary?
rationale: Exact-owner fail-closed behavior is the safer isolation rule, but it intentionally stops a previously permitted persisted-state workflow and repository policy requires explicit ownership of that compatibility/security tradeoff.

options.title: Fail closed for ownerless rows
options.body: Require exact owner equality and leave legacy ownerless rows manageable only by operators or non-plugin clients until deliberately migrated.

options.title: Add operator migration
options.body: Keep runtime fail-closed while providing a narrow doctor or administrative reassignment path for legitimate legacy plugin sessions.

options.title: Preserve ownerless access
options.body: Continue allowing plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, retaining compatibility but leaving plugin authority ambiguous.

recommendation.title: Fail closed for ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Require exact owner equality and leave legacy ownerless rows manageable only by operators or non-plugin clients until deliberately migrated.

likelyOwner.reason: The current projection/store boundary changed by this PR is directly attributable to his recent commit, making him the strongest evidence-backed owner for the exact ordering and compatibility choice.
